text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Kohl and Chirac want to boost fight against organised crime in EU
- German-Czech declaration to be initialled in this month
- Number of bankruptcies rose again in September
- Bank employees to get full sick pay
- FAZ indicator shows economy recovering further
- Engineering employers' chairman Werner Stumpfe wants tougher regulation of strikes
HANDELSBLATT
- Differences remain between France and Germany on EMU stability pact
- Experts say drop in financial markets was overreaction
- Engineering industry set to clinch pay settlement
- VW and GM aim for settlement in Lopez dispute
- Pressure mounts on Mercedes-Benz boss Helmut Werner to accept corporate restructuring
- Potash Corp of Saskatchewan (PCS) buys Kali und Salz majority stake from BASF
- Brussels investigation into subsidies for east German shipyards goes ever deeper
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bank employees secure full payment of sick pay
- French ex-interior minister Pasqua criticises German efforts to tackle international terrorism
- Engineering employers' chairman Stumpfe wants alternative to strikes for settling labour disputes
- Service sector wants to maintain contribution-free 590-mark jobs
- DAG union and Lufthansa make third attempt to settle pay dispute
DIE WELT
- Kohl rejects idea of toughening strike law
- Waigel says coalition parties may not unveil tax reform plan until early next year
- Declaration text says Prague regrets wrong done to expelled Sudeten Germans; declaration to be initialled on December 20
- VW chief executive Piech ready to apologise to GM in Lopez affair
- OECD report says Germans spend too long studying
- Bonn and Paris divided over single currency policy
- Haggling goes on in engineering industry pay talks
- Bankruptcies to hit new record
- European Patent Office slashes fees
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
